paragraph.text: EldenNet lets characters of the game hold a free conversation with you, in their own voice, written by an AI model you choose. It reads the game and never changes it, and works only offline, alone in your own world.
System › Status › Compatibility says whether this version of EldenNet supports your game's build, and which GraceUI it needs.
EldenNet is free software under the MIT License, developed with AI assistance. Its engine follows the logic and structure of SkyrimNet, whose author permits EldenNet to build on it:
EldenNet is not affiliated with or endorsed by FromSoftware or Bandai Namco.

EldenNet lets characters of the game hold a conversation with you. You type a line; the character answers in their own voice, in text on screen, written by an AI model that you choose. This page takes you from a fresh install to your first conversation.

list.text: answer when you speak to them. In this version the list is short.
Each of them has a profile EldenNet wrote in its own words, and knows what anyone would know on first meeting them.
You can add notes of your own on how a character speaks, on the same page under
Conversation is in text, in a box on screen. Characters only talk: they take no other action.
EldenNet reads the game and never changes it. It writes nothing into the game, and it never edits your saves.

blocks.heading: What it does not do yet

list.text: Other characters, soldiers and passers-by say nothing.
Characters do not speak up on their own, greet you or talk among themselves.
Nothing is remembered once the game closes. Within a session, a character recalls the last lines of your previous conversation with them.
There are no voices: lines are text only.
Some parts of the menu have no pages yet, and are not shown.
Playing on a Steam Deck or under Proton is not covered by this version.
The game on PC, through Steam. EldenNet works only offline, alone in your own world, without Easy Anti-Cheat, and its launcher starts the game that way.
GraceUI, the menu and on-screen layer EldenNet draws through. It comes with EldenNet.
An AI provider. It can be a cloud service, with a key of your own from that service (which may charge for its use), or a model server on this PC, or one on another PC of your home network.
Installing and starting EldenNet, and updating GraceUI
. The first time, read the notices it shows before the game starts.
. The menu is also in your browser while the game runs: GraceUI › Browser view gives its address.
, read the Status card: its State and Why rows say how EldenNet stands. It cannot read Speaking until a model answers.
, choose a preset, or keep the one shown. A preset chooses a model for each job.
, then paste your key on its row. For a server of your own, fill in a name and a base URL under
instead: a server on this PC, or one on your home network by its private address, takes no key. Then press
. It takes a few seconds and works at the title screen too. Its verdict says whether replies will come quickly enough.
